newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas prices firm on weather, doubts remain.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas prices firm on weather, doubts remain.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices, helped by forecasts for colder weather next week, firmed Wednesday, but many doubted the market's ability to sustain a rally, with stocks ample and winter drawing to a close.
While Northeast and Midwest temperatures are soon expected to dip, traders said a growing stock surplus, particularly in the East, should continue to plague the market.

"The reality of the market hasn't hit yet, but it will when utilities start going full bore on withdrawals and there's no demand," said one Texas trader, noting Gulf Coast cash prices were up 10-12 cents today to about $1.90/mmBtu.

But despite today's gain, Gulf prices were still about $1 below February indices, and traders saw little hope for a sustained rally near-term, as storage operators step up the pace of withdrawals later this month and next to get stocks down to more normal levels.
"The weather next week doesn't matter much. Everyone's comfortable with stocks," another Texas trader said.
A Reuter poll showed most expected a 110-125 bcf weekly stock draw when AGA releases its report later today.
In south Texas, prices also gained about a dime to the low-$1.80s but were still about 95 cents below Feb 1 levels.
Permian gas firmed by about five cents to the mid-to-high $1.60s, still 90 cents below index, while southern California border was up slightly to the low-$1.70s.
Midcontinent prices climbed by about 12 cents to the mid-$1.70s, helped by forecasts for colder weekend weather, but levels remained about $1 below Feb indices.
In the East, New York city-gate prices held relatively steady in the $2.15-2.20 range.
